sourceBasis: Wisconsin DNR statewide cross-country skiing inventory

regionAdditions.name: St. Croix / Western Wisconsin
regionAdditions.blurb: St. Croix River and western Wisconsin systems where storm track, colder inland nights and Twin Cities access create their own ski decisions.

regionAdditions.name: Driftless / Mississippi River
regionAdditions.blurb: Coulee and Mississippi bluff skiing from Trempealeau to Wyalusing, with steep terrain and highly variable freeze-thaw windows.

regionAdditions.name: Lake Michigan / Fox Valley
regionAdditions.blurb: Lakeshore and Fox Valley systems where lake moderation, wind and thinner natural-snow windows make timing especially important.

faqAdditions.q: How broad is the Wisconsin board now?
faqAdditions.a: The board includes destination Nordic centers plus a deep layer of Wisconsin DNR parks, forests and trails. State properties are screened with the same snow and surface engine, while Wisconsin DNR and Travel Wisconsin remain the authority for grooming and closure status.

faqAdditions.q: Why are some Wisconsin weather points property-level rather than exact trailheads?
faqAdditions.a: Large forests and parks can have several trailheads. The modeled weather point represents the ski property or trail system and is not intended as survey-grade trailhead GPS.

trails.name: Big Foot Beach State Park
trails.description: A southern Wisconsin classic-groomed state-park option near Lake Geneva, useful when a regional storm briefly opens a ski window close to the Illinois line.

trails.name: Black River State Forest
trails.description: A large western Wisconsin state-forest system with substantial classic and skate-groomed mileage and a warming shelter near the Highway O trailhead.

trails.name: Brunet Island State Park
trails.description: Classic-groomed skiing in Chippewa County, adding a colder north-central state-park option between Eau Claire and the Northwoods.

trails.name: Buckhorn State Park
trails.description: A central Wisconsin state-park classic system groomed when snow and staffing allow, making source freshness important before a drive.

trails.name: Capital Springs State Recreation Area
trails.pass: State or Dane County ski permit rules apply
trails.description: Madison-area classic and skate grooming where short natural-snow windows and rapid thaw cycles make same-day timing especially valuable.

trails.name: Flambeau River State Forest
trails.description: A remote Northwoods forest with combined classic and skate grooming where colder interior temperatures often preserve snow well.

trails.name: Governor Dodge State Park
trails.description: More than 12 miles of groomed classic terrain across the rolling Driftless edge near Dodgeville, with elevation and thaw timing both influencing the day.

trails.name: Governor Earl Peshtigo River State Forest
trails.description: A northeast Wisconsin forest system near Crivitz with combined classic and skate grooming and colder inland conditions than the lakeshore.

trails.name: Governor Knowles State Forest
trails.description: Classic-groomed western Wisconsin loops near the St. Croix River, useful for comparing northwest Wisconsin snow with the Twin Cities side of the border.

trails.name: Governor Nelson State Park
trails.description: Madison-area classic and skate skiing along Lake Mendota, where lake moderation can make surface timing differ from higher terrain west of the city.

trails.name: Governor Thompson State Park
trails.description: Groomed loops and additional packed winter routes in northeast Wisconsin, with a warming shelter and a strong natural-snow dependence.

trails.name: Harrington Beach State Park
trails.description: Classic-groomed Lake Michigan shoreline skiing where wind, lake moderation and thin-snow windows can change conditions quickly.

trails.name: Hartman Creek State Park
trails.description: Central Wisconsin state-park skiing with both classic and skate grooming, positioned between Fox Valley and colder interior snow belts.

trails.name: High Cliff State Park
trails.description: Classic-groomed park trails plus skate-groomed campground roads above Lake Winnebago, where wind and open exposure can matter.

trails.name: Hoffman Hills State Recreation Area
trails.description: Rolling western Wisconsin classic and skate terrain west of Menomonie, useful for tracking storms entering from Minnesota.

trails.name: Interstate State Park
trails.description: Classic-groomed skiing above the St. Croix gorge, directly useful for comparing western Wisconsin and eastern Minnesota snow windows.

trails.name: Kettle Moraine - Pike Lake Unit
trails.description: A compact Kettle Moraine classic and skate system near Hartford, highly dependent on southern Wisconsin snowfall and preservation.

trails.name: Kinnickinnic State Park
trails.description: Classic-groomed loops plus packed multi-use winter mileage near the St. Croix, serving the western Wisconsin metro fringe.

trails.name: Kohler-Andrae State Park
trails.description: Classic-groomed shoreline skiing south of Sheboygan where Lake Michigan wind and temperature moderation shape the ski window.

trails.name: Lake Kegonsa State Park
trails.description: A Madison-area classic and skate state-park system whose season is driven by short natural-snow opportunities and freeze-thaw timing.

trails.name: Mirror Lake State Park
trails.description: A substantial classic and skate system near Wisconsin Dells with protected forest terrain and more mileage than many southern state parks.

trails.name: NHAL - Escanaba Trail System
trails.description: One of the Northern Highland-American Legion State Forest's major groomed systems, with reliable cold and deep Northwoods forest cover.

trails.name: NHAL - McNaughton Trail System
trails.description: A groomed Northern Highland-American Legion forest network near Lake Tomahawk, valuable for Northwoods condition comparisons.

trails.name: Pattison State Park
trails.description: Classic-groomed skiing south of Superior in one of Wisconsin's coldest and snowiest corners, influenced by Lake Superior storms.

trails.name: Perrot State Park
trails.description: Mississippi River bluff skiing with classic grooming and limited skate mileage, making temperature swings and sun exposure important.

trails.name: Point Beach State Forest
trails.description: Lake Michigan state-forest skiing with both classic and skate grooming and a shelter near Two Rivers.

trails.name: Potawatomi State Park
trails.description: A Door County classic and skate system near Sturgeon Bay, complementing Peninsula and Whitefish Dunes for local snow comparisons.

trails.name: Red Cedar State Trail
trails.description: A linear trail south from Menomonie with groomed classic and skate skiing, useful when western Wisconsin gets a favorable storm track.

trails.name: Whitefish Dunes State Park
trails.description: Classic skiing over Door County dune and forest terrain on the Lake Michigan side of the peninsula.

trails.name: Wildcat Mountain State Park
trails.description: Driftless hill-country skiing with classic and skate grooming, where elevation and steep terrain amplify freeze-thaw effects.

trails.name: Willow River State Park
trails.description: A substantial classic and skate system east of St. Paul, making it one of the most useful cross-border condition comparisons in the network.

trails.name: Wyalusing State Park
trails.description: Far southwest Wisconsin bluff-country skiing above the Mississippi and Wisconsin rivers, strongly dependent on episodic snow windows.

trails.name: Yellowstone Lake State Park
trails.description: Classic-groomed southwest Wisconsin loops maintained as snow and staffing allow, making source freshness essential.
